record.paper_title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
record.original_question: Can any of the existing domination results currently relying on weak monotonicity of the spectral radius in the quotient algebra (see Sect. 4.2 in [ 14 ]) be proved without this condition? Maybe if the algebra cone in the original Banach algebra is assumed to be normal and/or generating? (This could allow these results to apply to other cases than the regular operators.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a complex unital Banach algebra. A non-empty subset $C \subseteq A$ is called an algebra cone if it contains the unit, is closed under addition, multiplication, and multiplication by non-negative scalars, and satisfies $C \cap (-C) = \{0\}$. The cone $C$ induces a partial order on $A$ by $a \le b \iff b - a \in C$. The cone $C$ is called normal if there exists a constant $\alpha > 0$ such that $0 \le a \le b$ implies $\|a\| \le \alpha \|b\|$, and generating if $A = C - C$. Let $r(\cdot)$ denote the spectral radius in $A$. Given a closed inessential ideal $I \subseteq A$, write $A/I$ for the quotient Banach algebra with quotient cone $C/I$, and let $r_{A/I}$ denote its spectral radius. The spectral radius is said to be weakly monotone on $C/I$ if $0 \le x \le y$ in $A/I$ implies $r_{A/I}(x) \le r_{A/I}(y)$.

A typical "domination" theorem in this setting asserts: if $0 \le a \le b$ in $A$, $b$ has some prescribed spectral or ergodic property (for instance, $b$ is Riesz, or ergodic, modulo $I$), and the spectral radius is weakly monotone on $C/I$, then $a$ inherits the corresponding property.

Question: Can such domination theorems be established without assuming weak monotonicity of the spectral radius in the quotient algebra $A/I$, replacing this hypothesis by structural assumptions on the cone $C$ in $A$ itself—specifically, that $C$ is normal, generating, or both?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on ordered Banach algebras. Recent works (2022–2025) on ergodic domination and generalized ergodic domination continue to assume weak monotonicity of the spectral radius in quotient algebras as a hypothesis, indicating the question remains open, though partial extensions exist in restricted settings (e.g., disjunctive products).

status_evidence.title: Ergodic domination in ordered Banach algebras with disjunctive products
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results on ergodic domination still rely on or refine the weak spectral radius monotonicity hypothesis in quotient algebras.
status_evidence.claim: The condition continues to be a standing assumption in domination results in OBAs.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Ergodic Domination in Ordered Banach Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Open question of whether the Ergodic Domination Theorem can be proved without assuming weak monotonicity in the quotient algebra A/I.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of removing the weak monotonicity assumption is acknowledged as open.

status_evidence.title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists domination without weak spectral monotonicity as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in the OBA literature.
